title: Edge chromatic number of an odd-order regular graph
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph whose number of vertices is odd, and suppose $G$ is $k$-regular for some integer $k \ge 1$ (every vertex has exactly $k$ neighbours). Then the edge chromatic number of $G$ — equivalently, the chromatic number of its line graph — equals $\Delta(G) + 1$, where $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$. Writing $\chi'(G)$ for the edge chromatic number, \[\chi'(G) = \Delta(G) + 1.\]
